title: Ormanetto (nuncio in Spain) to Cardinal of Como, 1573: copy of Philip II's letter with two cipher passages (ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 7; DECODE R116)

steps.what: Downloaded the DECODE images, the address leaf and the KL transcription of R116 with the session cookie.
Read the clear frame: a copy of Philip II's letter to the bishop of Padua (Ormanetto); address leaf to the Cardinal of Como, docketed 17 June 1573. DECODE's '7 Jan 1573' is the volume heading.
Ran Lasry's 1568 Spain nunciature polyphonic key (targets/alessandrino1568/decrypt.py).
Simple/homophonic substitution over three sign sets, Spanish and Italian 4-gram annealing.
Solver check on a known text: first quadgram solver failed its own control; replaced by the KL-penalised annealer, which reads a same-length Italian homophonic control.
Dandini-frame structure (2-digit letters with even second digit, 3 digits + mark as codes); pair-parity test per line.
Web and PARES search for a printed edition or the King's minute; Carini 1894 located but not online; PARES has only 1575 Ormanetto items.
Meister 1906, Ottoboniana collection 1573-87: found the Como keys with Spain nomenclator and the rules of the Spain nuncio's ordinary cipher.
Decoded with Meister VI.1 (Como, Spain nomenclator), Crivelli 1561 polyphonic key, and checked VI.2/VI.3 structure.
Polyphonic digit = two letters with unknown pairs, annealed; also with 1 as null and 0 as letter.
Same polyphonic annealer on 1,100 digits of Alessandrino R97 recovers 7 of 9 of Lasry's pairs (-2.18/char); R116 scores worse and restarts disagree.
Pooled R116 with R118 (1,660 signs; 4t = barred 4) and reran the polyphonic annealer.
Academic catalogues for an edition of Ormanetto's nunciature: Fernández Terricabras 2000 (no full text online); no register edition found.
Tomokiyo's cryptiana pages on papal and Spanish ciphers: no Ormanetto item, no decipherment.
Spanish royal-cipher syllabic structure (base digit + dot/mark vowel indicator), annealed in Spanish and Italian.

Outside key: A. Devadas (with Claude) emailed his reconstruction of the Spain nunciature's cifra ordinaria, built from this project's published images and ciphertext files, with a report of the reading of R116 and R118.

Rebuilt the decoder from the key description (dec_aj.py) and applied it to our own r116_cipher.txt: both passages read as Italian (ho visto il foglio mandatomi a parte sopra le cose di Pitigliano ...).
Italian per-letter score of the decode with the 16 well-supported code groups: -3.02 against a best of -6.69 over 200 letter-shuffled keys (mean -8.50).
The same key reads R118 (ormanetto1576), whose leaf carries the contemporary decipherment; the dateline and the 'qua' syllable group agree.
Code values graded by AJ kept as he graded them; the guessed and open groups (about a dozen) were not adopted without a second context.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The Spain nunciature's cifra ordinaria, reconstructed by A. Devadas from R116 and R118 and emailed on 1 Oct 2026, was applied to this project's transcription of R116 and reads both passages as Italian; checked by a shuffled-key control and by the same key reading R118.

gaps.item: about fifteen code groups in A and B (32, 288, 53, 422 ... )
gaps.detail: one or two contexts each; AJ's guesses not adopted without a second source

gaps.item: five suspect signs (ofrti, pbrticular, desi?bera, dol, a stray 1)
gaps.detail: local slips by the encipherer or the transcriber, to check on ff. 303r-304r

outcome.notes: Estimate from AJ's count (112 of 139 non-code words ordinary Italian), not re-measured here. Italian, not Spanish: passage A is Philip II on the league and the Emperor, B on Pitigliano. Pitigliano not checked against 1573 sources.

prior.where: No earlier reading known; the reading is A. Devadas's of 1 Oct 2026, made from this project's published files after the 21 Sept attempt.

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded. On 1 Oct 2026 an outside solver (A. Devadas) emailed a key; the owner asked the model to verify it against the project's own transcription and to write it up.
